FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE May 27, 2026 Media Contact: Melissa Mione 208-946-7730 | info@treasurevalleypartnership.org MEDIA ADVISORY Treasure Valley Leaders to Announce Regional Greenbelt Safety Initiative Officials to discuss collaborative effort focused on education, safety, and appropriate use GARDEN CITY, ID — As warmer weather brings more people onto the Boise River Greenbelt, leaders from the Treasure Valley Partnership (TVP) will hold a joint news conference to announce a regional Greenbelt safety and education initiative ahead of the busy summer recreation season. The coordinated effort focuses on promoting safe shared use of the Boise River Greenbelt and educating the public about which electric vehicles are permitted on the pathway system. New signage is being installed along the Greenbelt, starting in the Garden City region, to reinforce safety expectations and remind users that high-powered electric dirt bikes and motocross-style vehicles are not permitted on the Greenbelt. NEWS CONFERENCE DETAILS WHAT: TVP Greenbelt Safety & Etiquette News Conference WHO: Garden City Mayor Bill Jacobs, Eagle Mayor Brad Pike, Boise Mayor Lauren McLean, Meridian Mayor Robert Simison, Star Mayor Trevor Chadwick, Middleton Mayor Tim O’Meara, Ada County Commissioner Rod Beck, and Ada County Commissioner Ryan Davidson will be in attendance. Media personnel and interested community members are welcome and encouraged to attend. WHEN: Friday, May 29, 2026 at 1:30 pm MT WHERE: Garden City City Hall – courtyard next to Greenbelt Path | 6015 N Glenwood St, Garden City, ID 83714 “Most people want to do the right thing; they just may not realize that some of these high-powered, motorbike-style vehicles that can be found in many local retail shops aren’t allowed on the Greenbelt,” said Garden City Mayor Bill Jacobs. “This initiative is about community safety. If we all slow down, stay aware, and respect the space, the Greenbelt remains one of the best shared amenities in our region.” Media attending the event will have opportunities to capture footage of the new Greenbelt safety signage, recreational activity along the pathway, and interviews with local elected officials. Visual examples of permitted and prohibited electric vehicles may also be available as part of the public education effort. ### ABOUT THE TREASURE VALLEY PARTNERSHIP The Treasure Valley Partnership (TVP) unites cities and counties in Idaho’s most populous region to address shared challenges in tax policy, public safety, and infrastructure, all while advocating for local control and responsible growth. We’re a unified voice focused on practical solutions — ensuring growth pays for growth, protecting residents, and using taxpayer dollars wisely.
